correctness.rationale: For all prime powers q (including characteristic 2), the first two commutator equations aB=Ab and bC=Bc must hold, while the last scalar K=aE+dC-Ae-Dc changes under conjugation by the linear form B(aw+cu)-v(aC+cA). The image is zero or all of F_q; seven disjoint primary configurations count q^4 versus q^3 admissible middle entries. Summation yields rho=(2q^5-3q^4+3q^3+2q^2-4q+1)/q^7 and cp=(2q^2+q-2)/q^5 with strictly positive gap. Independently enumerated every relevant primary and middle entry for q=2 and 3, reproducing both ordered counts; no characteristic-specific division occurs.

originality.rationale: Britnell-Wildon introduced the classwise commuting relation and Blackburn-Britnell-Wildon the probability rho, specializing elsewhere (especially symmetric groups). Kaur-Sharma-Singh study ordinary commuting probabilities and branching in UT4, not whether separately chosen conjugates commute. Resultary search found related UT4 centralizer and commuting tuples but no matching conjugate-relaxed rho polynomial. An unresolved discrepancy for the companion ordinary cp in the Kaur table is explicitly recorded, not glossed over.
residual_risks: The published Section 8 ordinary-commuting cp table disagrees with the elementary direct q=3 count; mathematical reconciliation or correction is unresolved.
A full conjugacy-class incidence table not located in searched literature could imply the rho formula.
Direct q=2,3 counts do not prove general q; the seven-row algebraic partition supplies the universal argument.
